release_notes:
• Dropping the scrubber on a part that is not loaded now holds exactly there: the old voice stops at once and playback continues from that spot the moment its bytes arrive — no drift back to the old position, no restart from the top of the song
• Loading is faster everywhere: the first chunk of a play or a seek is fetched at half the size, so the first sound arrives roughly twice as quickly, and a far seek on a song already on disk is served straight from the file instead of decoding the whole track first
• Continuous dragging is safe: rapid releases coalesce into one final seek, a stream that fails after a seek now lands on your drop position instead of the start of the song, and the seek watchdog no longer gives up while the engine is merely starvation-paused
• Audio focus: Musify asks Android for focus when it plays, so a call or another app like YouTube now pauses it — a call ending resumes, YouTube does not — and unplugging headphones pauses too
